facts.text: Japanese nickname アフロディ (Afurodi), the name used for the character in the codex and in game text.
Japanese epithet アフロディ帝 ('Emperor Aphrodi'), used by other characters in game event ev15_01600.
In Inazuma Eleven Cross he is Shin Aphrodi (シン・アフロディ, 'God Aphrodi').
English localisation in Victory Road: name Byron Love, nickname Aphrody.
Community romanisation of the Japanese name: Afuro Terumi, nickname Aphrodi (the spelling used by the owner and by the fan wiki).
Dub nickname Aphrodite in the anime and older games; Victory Road changed it to Aphrody.
English epithet 'Archon Aphrodite' in Victory Road event text (ev15_01600: 'What's Archon Aphrodite doing out there?').
The codex first listed the English name as 'Aphro Deetie'; after community backlash it was reverted to Byron Love, and earlier Victory Road credits still show 'Aphro Deetie'.

Titles: 'Ruler of the Sky' (天空の支配者, Ares anime, dub 'Sovereign of the Skies'); 'God of Field' (ゴッド・オブ・フィールド, Victory Road and Cross, dub 'God of the Pitch'); 'Deus Ex Machina' (デウス・エクス・マキナ, Shin Aphrodi in Cross).

デウス・エクス・マキナ

facts.text: Other languages present on the fan wiki: de, es, it, nl use the title Byron Love; vi uses Afuro Terumi.
The name comes from Aphrodite (アフロディーテ), Greek goddess of love and beauty, in line with the Zeus team's naming motif; the kanji 美 in 照美 means beauty.

i18n.fr: Le surnom renvoie à la déesse grecque Aphrodite ; le nom japonais est un calque phonétique de « Aphro ».

facts.text: Male.
Birthday is May 17.
Japanese and South Korean (dual); in Inazuma Eleven 3 he joins the Korean national team because he is Korean.

Codex numbers are 185 (Inazuma Eleven), 2625 (GO: Light / Shadow) and 4526 (Ares); the game database order is 166.
Three internal character codes, one per era: c01001900 (series IE1, base id 936881403), c05026590 (GO, 4233601308), c07080010 (Ares, 3389112235); series id 1659389071.
Player Universe constellation: Inazumis (FR Éclaris); the codex also lists Summitas (Inazuma Eleven and Ares forms) and Tornadrix (GO form).

Voice actors: Japanese Yuko Sanpei (the English wiki also lists Shouji Masayuki for Inazuma Eleven); English David Lee McInnis (anime), Lucien Dodge (US game), Griffin Burns (Ares anime); French Antoni Lo Presti (first voice), Valéry Benjilali (second), Olivier Premel (adult).

facts.text: The native learn_level numbers (0, 1, 13, 20, 30, 43) are slot values and do not equal the unlock levels the fan wiki prints for Victory Road (Hopping Trick 1, God Knows 13, Heaven's Time 20, God Break 30, Chaos Break 38, Time Boost 43 for the Zeus form).

Other techniques across the main games: The Ikaros, Sprint Warp, Olympus Harmony, White Hurricane, All Delete, Setsuna Boost, God Wind, Time Boost, Nekketsu Overdrive, Kick Plus 20; Fire Dragon forms use God Knows Kai and Heaven's Time Kai.
Anime and movie techniques: GGG Senjou no Aria (with Kira Hiroto and Iwato Takashi, Orion episode 30), Hokkyoku Guma 2gou (Orion episode 45), The Birth (movie).
Spin-off signatures: God Knows, God Break, Chaos Break, Heaven's Time (Strikers series); God Knows Impact and GGG Senjou no Aria (card games); God Knows Machina for Shin Aphrodi (Cross).
Aura Burning Overdrive (wap01001), rank 3001; the fan wiki lists a Nekketsu Overdrive at Lv 43, probably the same aura (unconfirmed), learned at slot 38.
Aura Instant Burst (wap01005), rank 3005, learned at slot 38.

Keshin and Mixi Max entries in Chrono Stone and Galaxy include Masaishou Bishop B (GO), Majin Pegasus Arc, Kodaishin Kukulkan, Shourai no Seiryuu; Mixi Max donors include Choi Chang-soo, Shindou Takuto, Yuri Averin; Afubuki is a Mix 'n' Match with Shawn Froste (reference only).
Kageyama Reiji picks him as captain of Zeus; the team drinks the Aqua of the Gods (French: Nectar des Dieux) to raise its physical ability.
Zeus beats Teikoku Gakuen 10-0 in the Football Frontier, injuring every Teikoku player except Kidou, who did not play because of a leg injury.
Before the final he tells Raimon that entering is futile; Zeus leads in the first half, then Endou masters Majin The Hand, stops God Knows, and Raimon wins 4-3.
Shocked by the defeat, he refuses the Aqua of the Gods and trains on his own.
In the Aliea Academy arc he asks Endou to let him join Raimon; after doubts he scores the first goal against Diamond Dust with the powered-up God Knows.
Against Chaos he tries to break the double defence Ignite Steal and Frozen Steal, is injured and collapses when Gran ends the match; he is hospitalised and helps Fubuki through his split personality.
He scouts Gazel and Burn for Korea's Fire Dragon (he is Korean) and faces Inazuma Japan in the Asia preliminary final.
He scores with God Break; the combination Chaos Break with Gazel and Burn is stopped by Endou's Ikari no Tettsui, Fire Dragon loses 4-3, and he wishes Inazuma Japan luck on the world stage.
He appears in episode 29 at the Fifth Sector base and becomes coach of Kidokawa Seishuu to stop its players from destroying themselves with violent football.
In episode 30 he sides neither with Fifth Sector nor with the Resistance; the match against Raimon is to show which path his team takes, and he trades a smile with Kidou.

Alone in a park, ashamed that Zeus's skill was called fake after the Aqua of the Gods leaked, he says he truly loves soccer and will take responsibility; a mysterious woman (Matsuzaka Kiyo) calls him a god in training.
In episode 14 he appears with Zeus (Ares) at the Football Frontier ceremony and faces the new Raimon.
In episode 15 he performs God Knows Impact; Zeus loses 3-2 and he says there are things you only gain by losing.
Passed over for the squad, he arrives in episode 29 as an extra forward (scouted by Kidou), says Inazuma Japan cannot win as it is, and sets up a 4 versus 4 game with Hiroto.
Against Navy Invader he uses Heaven's Time and God Knows Impact, trains Hiroto and Iwato (amusement park) for GGG Senjou no Aria, and Japan wins 4-3; the French wiki credits him with four goals.
Against Russia he supports Norika, fights on despite being paralysed by Yuri Rodina's band, and Japan loses.
In the movie's altered timeline Team Ogre beats Zeus 36-0 in the semi-final.
Three forms exist: Inazuma Eleven (Zeus, middle school grade 8), GO (adult coach of Kirkwood), Ares (Zeus, grade 9; 'Raimon's defeat fueled him to refine his game').
He returns to Endou and asks to join Raimon: 'Never again will I foolishly rely on ambrosia.'
As leader of Korea's Fire Dragon he tells Inazuma National they are not the players they were.
As Kirkwood's coach: 'Not for Fifth Sector, nor for the revolution. We'll fight for our own sakes.'

facts.text: Joining Fire Dragon because he is Korean implies Korean-Japanese dual nationality, consistent with his place in Inazuma Japan (Orion).
In the original anime he is the first character to break a goal net with a shot, and one of the players to score a hat-trick.
The GO design was first drawn with shorter chin-length hair before the ponytail was chosen; in GO he is exclusive to the Dark version.
In the Inazuma Soulmates 2011 poll (Animage, January 2012) he, Burn and Gazel placed 19th with 12 votes.
He appeared as an obtainable Yo-kai in the Level-5 collaboration with Yo-kai Watch Punipuni.
The nie fan-world build places an NPC 'Terumi Afuro (Aphrody)' in Kizuna Town with the role 'Architecte Celeste' and Wind element; this is product content, not canon.
